issues.description: The problem text requires a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (textual description), but the UML and the provided solution/template use a parameterless messageOnMilk() returning String. This is a method-parameter mismatch: students following the textual description will implement a different signature than the template/solution and the provided Main usage, leading to compilation/test failures or confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) update the problem statement text to require a parameterless method String messageOnMilk() (and update the textual example to "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), matching the UML, template Main usage, and solution; or (B) change the interface and all implementations (and any usages in Main/template) to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update the examples and tests to include the milkVolume in the returned string. Prefer option (A) if the intended UML/solution is correct.

issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the Milkable.messageOnMilk method: in the Part 2 textual description it is described as messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (mentioning a volume parameter and a specific return format), whereas the UML, template usage (Main.java) and the solution implement messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This mismatch between the described method signature and the provided template/UML/solution creates confusion for students about which signature to implement and may lead to compilation/test failures or wasted effort.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification: either (A) update the problem statement to specify messageOnMilk() with no parameters and the return format used in the UML/template/solution, or (B) change the template and solution to define messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all call sites (e.g., Main and Farm) accordingly. Recommended: keep messageOnMilk() without parameters (matching UML and template) and remove the double-parameter variant from the textual Part 2 to avoid ambiguity.
